newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian shares edge upwards in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian shares edge upwards in quiet trade.

text.p: Jordanian shares crept upwards on Sunday in lifeless trading dominated by market heavyweight Arab Bank.

The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index gained 0.39 percent to 166.69 points in trade worth 468,000 dinars ($660,000). Arab Bank, which rose 1.25 dinars to 294.25 dinars, accounted for one third of the turnover value.
Brokers say most local investors have kept out of the market but the Arab Bank gains and sustained international interest in blue chips helped sustain the index.
"There's a lack of local institutional buying, balanced by continuity of foreign interest in the phosphate and cement firms," said Mohammad Abdullah, senior analyst at Pearl Consulting.
Bank of Jordan and Jordan National Bank both attracted some interest but closed barely changed at 3.05 dinars and 2.05 dinars respectively.
Overall 10 shares rose on Sunday and eight fell, with another 17 trading but closing unchanged.
